site.name: pelagic
site.summary: pelagic-clone Marketing site (landing page) for the fictional open-source vector database Pelagic. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Single-page landing: top nav + animated GitHub-stars counter pill; hero with title, dual CTAs, `pip install` copy strip, rotating benchmark numbers, right-side 4-language (Python / Node / Go / curl) code tabs; Trusted-by logo row; 3 core-feature cards; Ingest → Index → Query three-step flow; architecture SVG diagram; customer quote cards; left Blog 5 posts + right Changelog 5 entries dual feed; 4-column footer with sitemap | | `styles.css` | Brand color #0E5C8A deep-sea blue; Inter + JetBrains Mono; responsive at 3 breakpoints (>1100 / 880–1100 / <880) | | `script.js` | Stars-counter 1.2s eased animation; code tabs switch Python / Node / Go / curl; benchmark rows rotate every 2.5s; `pip install pelagic` copy toast; fictional-logo rendering |

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore the Pelagic single-page marketing experience, validating the primary hero-to-information flow, interactive landing-page behaviors, section navigation, and responsive/mobile usability.
run_plan.summary: This run should treat index.html as a complete single-page product-marketing journey rather than a multi-page app. Start by validating the hero and top-nav conversion path, then exercise the page’s scripted interactions: code-language tabs, benchmark rotation, stars animation, and copy-to-clipboard toast. After that, inspect deeper content sections and footer links/anchors, then repeat critical conversion and navigation checks on mobile with special attention to the prescan’s small tap targets and responsive layout shifts.
assumptions: The site consists of a single known HTML page: index.html.
Most navigation appears to be in-page anchor navigation or placeholder links rather than real adjacent pages.
Interactive behavior is driven by script.js and includes stars-count animation, code-tab switching, benchmark rotation, and copy feedback.
Because no forms, dialogs, or additional HTML pages were seen, the run should focus on state changes, scroll/anchor behavior, and UX quality rather than submission flows.
risk_hotspots: Hero region on index.html: primary CTA pair (Quickstart, View on GitHub) and clarity of next-step hierarchy
Top navigation anchor links (Product, Docs, Pricing, Blog, Quickstart): risk of broken, misleading, or poorly aligned in-page jumps
Copy install command control: clipboard action and toast/confirmation visibility
Code sample language tabs (python/node/go/curl): risk of tabs not updating content or lacking clear active state
Rotating benchmark numbers: risk of distracting motion, unreadable transitions, or content shifting
Animated GitHub stars pill: risk of unnecessary motion or misleading affordance if it links nowhere meaningful
Footer sitemap/community links with href '#' placeholders: risk of dead-end interactions and expectation mismatch
Mobile header/nav and hero controls: multiple prescan small tap targets suggest touch usability issues

phases.title: Primary landing and hero flow
phases.objective: Validate the first-screen product pitch, CTA hierarchy, and immediate path from arrival to action.
key_checks: Confirm hero messaging, trust cue, and performance claims are visible and scannable on initial load
Activate Quickstart CTA in hero or header and verify whether it scrolls to a meaningful in-page destination
Activate View on GitHub and confirm whether it navigates meaningfully or behaves like a placeholder
Inspect the install strip and Copy control for obvious affordance and visibility near the CTAs
Assess whether the hero’s right-side code example supports rather than competes with the main conversion path
exit_criteria: Hero CTAs have been clicked and their outcomes observed
Initial-value proposition and next-step clarity are documented
Any dead-end or misleading hero interactions are confirmed

phases.title: Interactive scripted components
phases.objective: Exercise all visible JS-driven behaviors and confirm they are understandable, stable, and discoverable.
key_checks: Click each code tab (python, node, go, curl) and verify content updates correctly and active state is clear
Use the Copy install command button and verify clipboard feedback/toast appears, is readable, and dismisses appropriately
Observe benchmark rotation for at least one full cycle and check for jank, layout shift, or hard-to-read transitions
Observe GitHub stars counter animation on load or after refresh to confirm it completes smoothly and does not distract
Check whether any of these animated elements continue moving excessively or interfere with reading
exit_criteria: All four code tabs have been exercised
Copy interaction and resulting feedback have been verified
At least one rotation cycle and the stars animation have been observed and assessed

phases.title: In-page navigation and section continuity
phases.objective: Verify that the landing page supports smooth progression from hero through features, architecture, social proof, and content feeds.
key_checks: Use top-nav anchors (Product, Docs, Pricing, Blog, Quickstart) and confirm each lands at a sensible section or reveal any missing anchors
Scroll through feature cards, the Ingest → Index → Query sequence, architecture section, quote cards, and dual blog/changelog area to assess readability and narrative order
Check whether section headings and supporting text maintain hierarchy and avoid overly dense blocks
Inspect whether the blog and changelog feed items appear interactive, understandable, and visually balanced
Confirm that returning to the top or continuing downward feels coherent after anchor jumps
exit_criteria: All visible top-nav anchors have been tested
Core informational sections have been viewed in sequence
Any broken jumps, weak section labeling, or continuity issues are captured

phases.title: Footer and edge-link validation
phases.objective: Probe lower-priority but high-risk link affordances that may create dead ends or credibility issues.
key_checks: Test representative footer links across sitemap/docs/community columns such as Overview, Docs, Quickstart, GitHub, Discord, and Forum
Determine which footer links are placeholders versus meaningful navigation
Assess whether placeholder links are visually indistinguishable from real destinations
Check if footer layout remains legible and well grouped near the bottom of the long page
exit_criteria: A representative sample of footer links has been clicked
Footer IA and trust implications are documented

phases.title: Mobile-critical regression pass
phases.objective: Repeat the most important navigation and conversion checks in a mobile viewport, focusing on touch targets and responsive layout behavior.
key_checks: Review mobile header and above-the-fold hero for stacking, clipping, and CTA prominence
Retest top navigation access and any anchor-jump behavior on mobile
Retest Quickstart CTA, Copy control, and at least two code tabs on mobile
Check whether benchmark stats, trusted-by logos, feature cards, architecture graphic, and footer columns reflow cleanly
Pay special attention to the prescan small tap targets for nav items, tabs, stars pill, and copy control
exit_criteria: Critical conversion and navigation interactions have been repeated on mobile
Responsive reflow of major sections has been inspected
Touch-target and readability issues have been confirmed or ruled out

coverage_targets.pages: Visit the single known HTML page (index.html) and cover it from top to footer in both desktop and mobile viewports.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise all visible scripted features on index.html, all hero CTAs, all top-nav anchors, all code tabs, the copy action, and a representative sample of footer links.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical hero, navigation, copy, and tab interactions on mobile, plus inspect reflow of major content sections and all prescan-flagged small tap targets.

notes: Do not spend steps searching for non-existent pages unless a click clearly reveals one; the prescan only showed index.html.
Because many links appear to use '#' or in-page anchors, prioritize confirming actual outcomes over assuming intended destinations.
If anchor links fail or multiple links resolve to the same top-of-page position, treat that as a key UX finding rather than a navigation success.

observation.title: Pelagic — Open-source vector database
observation.visible_text: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Index build: 2.3× faster python node go curl from pelagic import Client db = Client("https://api.pelagic.dev", api_key="pk_live_…") index = db.create_index( name="docs", dim=1536, metric="cosine", hybrid=True, ) index.upsert([ {"id": "doc-001", "vector": embed(text), "filter": {"lang": "en"}} ]) hits = index.query( vector=embed("what is hnsw"), top_k=10, filter={"lang": "en"}, rerank="bge-large", ) 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Architecture Client SDKs py · node · go · rust Gateway auth · rate-limit · cache Coordinator routing · planner Shard 1 Shard 2 Shard 3 Object storage "We swapped our managed FAISS for self-hosted Pelagic in an afternoon. p95 fell from 91ms to 17ms, and we cut our retrieval bill by two-thirds. The migration tool re-indexed 240M vectors without a single drop." SF Sana Falconer Staff ML Engineer, Halcyon Health From the blog 2026-05-04 Why we rewrote our HNSW build in Rust A 1,400-line memory-allocator rewrite cut index build time by 2.3× — the postmortem. Marisol Chen 2026-04-21 Pelagic 0.42: hybrid search, done right Dense + sparse + filter in a single planner. The query language, the plan, the numbers. Aditya Rao 2026-04-02 One billion vectors on a single $400/mo box Tuning IVF-PQ and disk caching for the long tail of recall. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. New --ef-build-auto heuristic. Fixes a rare segfault on filtered queries with empty bitmaps. v0.42.0 Hybrid retrieval GA. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale. PRODUCT Overview Hybrid search Managed Pricing RESOURCES Docs Quickstart Benchmarks Migration guides COMMUNITY GitHub Discord Forum RFC tracker Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

observation.visible_text: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Throughput: 42k QPS python node go curl package main import "github.com/pelagic-io/pelagic-go" func main() { db := pelagic.New("pk_live_…") idx, _ := db.CreateIndex("docs", 1536, pelagic.Cosine, pelagic.Hybrid) idx.Upsert([]pelagic.Row{ {ID: "doc-001", Vector: embed(text), Filter: pelagic.M{"lang": "en"}}, }) hits, _ := idx.Query(pelagic.Q{ Vector: embed("what is hnsw"), TopK: 10, Filter: pelagic.M{"lang": "en"}, Rerank: "bge-large", }) _ = hits } 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. observation.title: Pelagic — Open-source vector database
observation.visible_text: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… p95 latency: 18ms python node go curl curl -X POST https://api.pelagic.dev/v1/indexes/docs/query \ -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_live_…" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "vector": [0.0123, -0.0876, ...], "top_k": 10, "filter": {"lang": "en"}, "rerank": "bge-large" }' 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Architecture Client SDKs py · node · go · rust Gateway auth · rate-limit · cache Coordinator routing · planner Shard 1 Shard 2 Shard 3 Object storage "We swapped our managed FAISS for self-hosted Pelagic in an afternoon. p95 fell from 91ms to 17ms, and we cut our retrieval bill by two-thirds. The migration tool re-indexed 240M vectors without a single drop." SF Sana Falconer Staff ML Engineer, Halcyon Health From the blog 2026-05-04 Why we rewrote our HNSW build in Rust A 1,400-line memory-allocator rewrite cut index build time by 2.3× — the postmortem. Marisol Chen 2026-04-21 Pelagic 0.42: hybrid search, done right Dense + sparse + filter in a single planner. The query language, the plan, the numbers. Aditya Rao 2026-04-02 One billion vectors on a single $400/mo box Tuning IVF-PQ and disk caching for the long tail of recall. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. New --ef-build-auto heuristic. Fixes a rare segfault on filtered queries with empty bitmaps. v0.42.0 Hybrid retrieval GA. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Recall@10: 0.987 python node go curl import { Pelagic } from "pelagic"; const db = new Pelagic({ apiKey: "pk_live_…" }); const index = await db.createIndex({ name: "docs", dim: 1536, metric: "cosine", hybrid: true, }); await index.upsert([ { id: "doc-001", vector: await embed(text), filter: { lang: "en" } }, ]); const hits = await index.query({ vector: await embed("what is hnsw"), topK: 10, filter: { lang: "en" }, rerank: "bge-large", }); 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Architecture Client SDKs py · node · go · rust Gateway auth · rate-limit · cache Coordinator routing · planner Shard 1 Shard 2 Shard 3 Object storage "We swapped our managed FAISS for self-hosted Pelagic in an afternoon. p95 fell from 91ms to 17ms, and we cut our retrieval bill by two-thirds. The migration tool re-indexed 240M vectors without a single drop." SF Sana Falconer Staff ML Engineer, Halcyon Health From the blog 2026-05-04 Why we rewrote our HNSW build in Rust A 1,400-line memory-allocator rewrite cut index build time by 2.3× — the postmortem. Marisol Chen 2026-04-21 Pelagic 0.42: hybrid search, done right Dense + sparse + filter in a single planner. The query language, the plan, the numbers. Aditya Rao 2026-04-02 One billion vectors on a single $400/mo box Tuning IVF-PQ and disk caching for the long tail of recall. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. New --ef-build-auto heuristic. Fixes a rare segfault on filtered queries with empty bitmaps. v0.42.0 Hybrid retrieval GA. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip.
